selected_modules.reason: The issue is explicitly a C++26 language feature request/bug area: "[C++26] P1306R5 - Expansion statements". All reproducers are in g++.dg/cpp26 and the expected diagnostics are C++ front-end semantic messages such as "'template for' only available with", structured-binding restrictions, name-independent declarations, and pack-indexing gating. Per module docs, gcc/cp owns C++ parsing, semantic analysis, templates, constexpr, diagnostics, and newer language features, making it the most direct upstream source for expansion-statement support and related diagnostics.

Several observed/expected failures are language-version and feature-gating diagnostics rather than optimizer/runtime failures, and gcc/c-family contains shared C-family option processing, pragma/attribute semantics, common tree helpers, and reusable diagnostics infrastructure used by C++. Since the reproducers hinge on standard-version availability checks and front-end shared diagnostics behavior, this shared layer is a strong adjacent module to inspect after gcc/cp.

Execution/log facts show the current compiler rejects -std=c++2c and -frange-for-ext-temps as unrecognized options. Even though that may reflect an older baseline, the feature area depends on option recognition and standard-mode plumbing. The options module owns declarative option definitions, parsing, aliases, and compiler-side option management, so it is relevant for the surface failure around unsupported C++26 mode spelling and related feature-enable switches.

The reproducers heavily involve structured bindings and decomposition-related semantics, and one related test (decomp64.C) fails with structured-binding compile errors before passes. Module docs indicate tree-core hosts core tree IR plus shared tree-level analyses/lowering including broad middle-end support for tree-based language constructs. If expansion statements introduce or reuse tree forms around structured bindings / for-range declarations, this module is a plausible intermediate representation layer beneath the C++ frontend.

selected_files.reason: Best upstream match for P1306R5 expansion statements. The issue and tests are centered on a new C++26 syntactic form ('template for') plus version-gating diagnostics such as "'template for' only available with". File docs identify parser.cc as the main recursive-descent parser that recognizes C++ grammar, extensions, tentative parsing, and builds the front-end nodes before later semantic checks. That makes it the most likely place for introducing/parsing expansion-statement syntax and issuing early dialect-availability errors.

Strong intermediate semantic candidate because expansion statements are statement-level constructs and the reproducer expectations include many context-sensitive declaration/statement diagnostics around for-range-declarations and structured bindings inside the new construct. File docs say semantics.cc is the general semantic-action layer used during parsing and template instantiation, building/finalizing many statement and expression forms and other cross-cutting semantic operations. This fits semantic construction/checking of a parsed expansion-statement node after parser recognition.

Likely source of several expected diagnostics about invalid declaration-specifiers on the for-range-declaration / structured-binding declaration within expansion statements: 'static', 'thread_local', '__thread', 'register', 'extern', 'mutable', 'typedef', 'consteval', 'constinit', 'inline', plus friend/virtual/explicit misuse. Docs describe decl.cc as the primary declaration-processing file that builds and validates declarations and enforces declaration semantics. Since many tests specifically probe declaration legality in the new statement form, decl.cc is a strong file-level match.

Important because the feature is specifically a 'template for' expansion statement and reproducer tags emphasize c++_templates, parameter-pack-related diagnostics, and pack indexing/name-independent declarations. File docs describe pt.cc as the core template processing/instantiation engine, including parameter-pack discovery and expansion plus instantiation of dependent statements and expressions. That makes it a plausible upstream/intermediate file for the template-pack semantics unique to expansion statements beyond basic parsing.

Per the file doc, c-opts.cc implements shared C/C++ option processing, selects language standards and dialect flags, and finalizes front-end/preprocessor setup. That makes it the most direct shared-layer file for C++26 mode plumbing and feature-enable option acceptance before C++-specific parsing/semantics even run.

Strong companion to c-opts.cc because the failures specifically mention option spellings being unrecognized. The doc says c.opt is the declarative option table for C/C++ front ends, defining switches, aliases, language masks, enums, and variable bindings used by GCC’s option-generation machinery. If -std=c++2c aliasing / standard-mode exposure or -frange-for-ext-temps recognition is missing at the shared C-family layer, this file is a primary source of that behavior.

Relevant shared semantic infrastructure file for the expected diagnostics that are standard-version gated rather than optimization-related, such as “structured bindings only available with”, “name-independent declarations only available with”, and “pack indexing only available with”. Its doc describes common C-family language option state, tree utilities, and front-end helper logic used before lowering. While the detailed expansion-statement semantics are likely in gcc/cp, this is one of the likeliest shared files in gcc/c-family to participate in common feature/version checks and reusable front-end state.

Most observed failures in this module scope are surface-trigger option-recognition failures: every cpp26 test currently dies on unrecognized ‘-std=c++2c’, and one also on unrecognized ‘-frange-for-ext-temps’.
